note: Curated first-party mods, fetched at runtime by TidePool. Editing this file changes what the Essentials tab shows without shipping a new app build - which is how a 'planned' entry becomes installable later.

mods.name: MelonLoader
mods.summary: The mod loader. Install this first - code mods need it.
mods.description:
MelonLoader is the loader that runs code mods, and it is the one that works on Surf Sandbox.

The game is Unity 6.3 (6000.3.8f1). BepInEx 6 does not run on it - the build Thunderstore ships never starts, and the newest development build loads its runtime and then spins indefinitely generating interop. MelonLoader 0.7.3 generates the same assemblies in about forty seconds and loads cleanly. Tested against the real game.

It installs into the game folder rather than a profile, because that is where it bootstraps from. First launch takes a minute while it generates assemblies, and it opens a console window that tells you what it is doing.

Beaches need no loader, so Break Pack works without this.

mods.name: SurfMP
mods.summary: Multiplayer for Surf Sandbox. Share a lineup with friends.
mods.description:
Adds multiplayer to Surf Sandbox: sit in the same lineup as your friends, watch each other take off, and trade waves.

The host runs the wave simulation and broadcasts it, so everyone is looking at the same ocean rather than hoping two machines drift to the same answer. Everything else - your surfer, your board, your position - is simulated locally and synced.

Uses Steam's peer-to-peer networking, so there is no port forwarding and no server to run. Invite through Steam and paddle out.

mods.name: Break Pack
mods.summary: Nine real waves, recreated from their actual sea-floor shape.
mods.description:
Pipeline, Teahupo'o, Nazare, Jeffreys Bay, Skeleton Bay, Mavericks, Puerto Escondido, Pleasure Point - and one gentle sandbar to learn on.

These are not drawn by eye. Each break is built from a cross-section of its real sea floor, because what a wave does is decided almost entirely by how fast the bottom rises underneath it. Teahupo'o goes from open ocean to half a metre of reef in about thirty metres, which is why it breaks below sea level. Skeleton Bay barely changes angle for a kilometre, which is why the rides never end.

Most profiles are stylised - they reproduce each wave's character rather than navigational depths. Pleasure Point is the exception: it is measured, sampled from NOAA's CUDEM model along the line a refracted swell actually travels into the point.

No loader needed: beaches are ordinary save files, so this installs and works without BepInEx.
